claims.exact_statement: For a finite birth-death chain on {0,...,M} with unit controlled births at predictable intensity at most B, death intensity gamma*n, and stationary mean m, a probability vector pi is implementable iff pi is nonnegative and normalized, has mean m, and satisfies gamma*(n+1)*pi[n+1] <= B*pi[n] for every n<M. The average accepted birth rate is exactly gamma*m. Therefore stationary dropout, second moment, and variance at a fixed mean have exact finite LP frontiers, with an average-translation cap C added as gamma*m<=C.
assumptions: gamma>0 and finite M
births add one molecule and are blocked at M
death rates are independent and linear in copy number
the controller has access to the count state for the constructive converse
stationary long-run law and costs
claims.status: internally proved exact model characterization; general LP method is established prior art
claims.novelty_boundary: Constrained-average CTMDP occupation-measure LPs and controlled birth-death examples are prior art. This is an exact model-specific adjacent-flow representation; novelty is not claimed.

claims.falsifier: A stationary law satisfying the displayed inequalities but not realizable by rates u_n=gamma*(n+1)*pi[n+1]/pi[n], or a realizable stationary law violating one inequality.

claims.exact_statement: At any finite-capacity LP vertex with positive support {0,...,L}, at most one edge inequality inside that support is strict. Thus an optimizer of any linear scalarization of fixed-mean dropout and variance can be chosen with peak birth rate B on all supported edges except at most one partial-rate edge, followed by a support cutoff.
assumptions: same single-output finite birth-death model as PB-C2-SINGLE-OUTPUT-FRONTIER
fixed mean
linear objective in stationary probabilities
claims.status: internal finite-dimensional extreme-point proof; external validation and priority unresolved
claims.novelty_boundary: The argument specializes a standard occupation-polytope perspective. The exact one-partial-edge statement was not established as novel by this bounded source check.
claims.falsifier: A vertex with two strict supported-edge inequalities under the stated fixed-mean polytope.

claims.exact_statement: For M=2, gamma=B=1, h=2, and mean m=1/2, the feasible law pi=(5/8,1/4,1/8), implemented by rates (2/5,1), has P(N<2)=7/8 and variance 1/2. Every standard single-cutoff policy at that mean has law (1/2,1/2,0), P(N<2)=1, and variance 1/4. Therefore a standard single-cutoff feedback rule is not globally optimal for this fixed-mean lower-tail objective.
assumptions: standard cutoff means peak rate below one cutoff, optionally one partial rate at the cutoff, then zero
stationary fixed-mean comparison
unit births, linear deaths, finite capacity
claims.status: exact rational counterexample; an independent rational active-set checker passes
claims.novelty_boundary: This refutes universal cutoff optimality for the stated tail objective only. Threshold policies under other queue reward and holding-cost objectives are established.

claims.exact_statement: For two binary outputs with equal death rate gamma and equal stationary marginal mean m, let d=P(N1=N2=1). For positive four-state masses, the least instantaneous shared unit-birth cap realizing d is B_exact(m,d)=gamma*max{d/(m-d), 2*(m-d)/(1-2*m+d)}. A state-feedback policy splitting births in state 00, filling the absent output in each singleton state, and producing nothing in state 11 attains the bound.
assumptions: state space {0,1}^2
independent unit deaths at rate gamma per present output
unit births with aggregate intensity at most B in every state
stationary equal marginals and positive state masses
full joint-state observation and zero-delay control for the construction
claims.status: exact model formula with constructive reversible attainment; novelty unknown
claims.novelty_boundary: General controlled birth-death and constrained-average CTMDP optimization are prior art. The exact two-output formula is a model-specific derivation; no priority claim is made.

claims.exact_statement: For the stated two-binary-output CTMC with Poisson perfect reads at rate nu and the specified held full-information action table, lifting the plant N and last-read state Y gives a 16-state CTMC whose stationary law can be solved directly. The slow-read limit has P(N=11)=(6-sqrt(34))/24 and each mean (8-sqrt(34))/24; the fast-read limit recovers P(N=11)=(6-sqrt(34))/10 and means 0.1. A 50-digit solve at delta=nu/gamma=1.3220897723 gives P(N=11)=0.01238479537 and each mean 0.09559063552. The numerical ratio (P_delta(N=11)-0.01)/delta has a candidate maximum 0.001803807443 near that delta, but this is not a certified global optimization over observation rates or policies.
assumptions: two binary outputs with independent unit death rate after normalization by gamma
perfect instantaneous Poisson reads independent of the plant
memory stores the last full joint state
actions are held between reads using the fixed table specified in SAMPLE_HOLD_16STATE.md
reads incur fixed per-read cost and are charged even when the memory already equals the plant state
claims.status: internally reproducible 16-state stationary CTMC calculation with analytic endpoint limits; cost-ratio maximum is numerically located, not globally certified
claims.novelty_boundary: Controlled observation in CTMDPs is established prior art. This fixed-rate, fixed-table calculation is a model-specific stationary diagnostic, not a new observation-control theorem and not a globally optimized partially observed controller.

prior_art_status.ctmdp_and_queues: Constrained average CTMDP occupation LPs for history-dependent policies and controlled birth-death examples are established prior art: Guo, Huang, and Song (2012), DOI 10.1137/100805169. Controlled queues and birth-death processes with objective-specific monotone policies and LP methods are also prior art: Serfozo (1981), DOI 10.2307/1426467.
prior_art_status.molecular_feedback: Resource-aware genetic-circuit controllers and antithetic noise-control strategies are established: Nature Communications 2018, DOI 10.1038/s41467-018-02898-6; Chakravarty, Zhang, and Tian (2024), DOI 10.1109/cdc56724.2024.10886586. Resource-constrained spatial gene-expression optimization is established in Sokolowski et al. (2025), DOI 10.1073/pnas.2402925121.
prior_art_status.novelty: No exhaustive priority search was performed. All claims are model-specific or standard mathematical specializations; novelty remains unknown.

next_decisive_gate: Build or select a specific molecular or instrumented two-output allocator, include controller and resource species in the CTMC, estimate shared translation cap, per-output degradation, state-observation channel, latency, growth dilution, and per-read/controller resource cost, then compare matched peak-and-average-cost reliability against the constant split and full-state LP bound. The p=0.1 example has only 0.01878 translation-rate units of full-information peak advantage and requires 0.4 average joint-state reads per unit time.
